text: Investigating the relativedelta float-addition bug now (locating the exact code path and checking the test baseline). Baseline: full suite green (1064 passed, 43 skipped). ETA for the fix: ~8 minutes.
Got it — looking at the rrule `count=0` handling now, in parallel with the relativedelta fix. ETA: ~10 minutes.
Noted — investigating the rrule `__str__`/RRULE token issue as well. ETA: ~12 minutes.
Noted — investigating the parser `fuzzy_with_tokens` issue now. ETA: ~12 minutes.

Fixed. `rrule._iter` used a truthiness test (`if count:`) so `count=0` was treated as "no limit" and the generator ran to year 9999. Both branches now decrement before yielding and stop at `count < 0`, so `rrule(DAILY, count=0, dtstart=...)` yields `[]` and `.count()` returns 0, while `count=1/2/3` and `count=None` are unchanged. Verified: test_rrule.py 542 passed, full suite 1064 passed / 43 skipped (no regressions).
Noted — investigating the parser `test_idx_check` bug (index handling) now. ETA: ~12 minutes.
Noted — investigating the relativedelta absolute-attribute addition bug (`testAbsoluteAddition`) now. ETA: ~12 minutes.

Fixed. In `parser._parse`, the `elif idx == 2:` branch (the `X m SS` case) was indented inside the `if value % 1:` block nested under `if idx == 1:`, making it dead code, so the seconds/microseconds of a trailing number were dropped (e.g. `parse('10 m 36')` gave 00:10:00 instead of 00:10:36). Dedented it one level to pair with `if idx == 1:`. Verified: test_parser.py 175 passed, full suite 1064 passed / 43 skipped (no regressions).

Fixed. `rrule.__str__` built the rule body but never emitted the `RRULE:` token, so `str(rrule(DAILY, count=5, dtstart=datetime(2000,1,1)))` returned `'DTSTART:20000101T000000
FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=5'`. It now returns `'DTSTART:20000101T000000
RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=5'` (and `'...
RRULE:FREQ=DAILY'` with no dtstart); round-trips through `rrulestr` still work. Verified: test_rrule.py 542 passed, full suite 1064 passed / 43 skipped (no regressions).
